title.value: Cross-Validation for Training and Testing Co-occurrence Network Inference Algorithms
title.justification: The title directly reflects the central topic of the paper, which is introducing a new method for training and testing network inference algorithms using cross-validation.
title.quote: Cross-Validation for Training and Testing Co-occurrence Network Inference Algorithms

analysis.description: The paper proposes a novel cross-validation method for evaluating co-occurrence network inference algorithms in microbial ecological data, focusing on the hyper-parameter selection and comparison of algorithm quality. It introduces new methods for applying existing algorithms to predict on test data, specifically in the context of microbial networks.

type.justification: The study includes empirical testing and analysis of different algorithms using real microbiome datasets, demonstrating the application of the proposed cross-validation methods to infer network associations.
type.quote: Our empirical study shows that the proposed method is useful for hyper-parameter selection (training) and comparing the quality of the inferred networks between different algorithms (testing).

name.justification: The research focuses on computational methods for analyzing biological data, specifically microbial communities, which falls under Computational Biology.
name.quote: Understanding the ecological interactions that occur in microbial communities is very crucial in maintaining a well-functioning ecosystem.

name.justification: The focus is on understanding the interactions and associations within microbial communities using computational methods.
name.quote: Co-occurrence network inference algorithms help us understand the complex associations of micro-organisms, especially bacteria.

name.justification: The paper deals with machine learning techniques such as cross-validation and algorithms like LASSO and GGM for network inference.
name.quote: Cross-validation is a standard algorithm in machine learning used for selection, evaluation and estimation of performance of models.

name.justification: LASSO is frequently mentioned as one of the algorithms used for co-occurrence network inference and is explicitly described in its application and comparison.
name.quote: LASSO uses the degree of L1 regularization, typically selected using cross-validation to determine the sparsity of the network.

is_contributed.justification: The paper does not claim to have developed LASSO but uses it as part of their comparative study and application to test new methods.
is_contributed.quote: Cross-validation has been used previously in training LASSO using validation error.

is_executed.justification: LASSO is explicitly described in the analysis and execution as part of the validation and testing against microbiome data.
is_executed.quote: We specifically utilized the LassoCV...to implement the LASSO algorithm and estimate the precision matrix for the GGM respectively.

is_compared.justification: LASSO is compared numerically with other algorithms throughout the paper, including GGM and correlation methods.
is_compared.quote: The LASSO outperformed the other algorithms on the iOral data set.

referenced_paper_title.value: Regression Shrinkage and Selection Via the Lasso
referenced_paper_title.justification: This is the classic reference title for LASSO cited throughout the research field to refer to the original method.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Tibshirani, R. Regression Shrinkage and Selection Via the Lasso, 1996.

name.justification: GGM is frequently analyzed and leveraged for inference of microbial ecological interactions and is prominently discussed in the methods and results.
name.quote: The GGM outperformed the other algorithms on the iOral data set.

is_contributed.justification: GGM itself is not contributed by the paper; it is used as an existing model to test new methodologies.
is_contributed.quote: Similarly, it has also been used in training Gaussian Graphical Models(GGM) for inferring a sparse inverse covariance matrix.

is_executed.justification: The paper employs GGM for empirical analysis and network inference testing in the context of microbiome data.
is_executed.quote: The GGM outperformed the other algorithms on the iOral data set.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares GGM with other network inference algorithms as part of their study.
is_compared.quote: For the Amgut1 data set, GGM achieved the highest accuracy from 10 to 20 sample size.

referenced_paper_title.value: Conditional Dependence Network Inference for Compositional Data
referenced_paper_title.justification: The GGM method is generally linked to works that discuss graphical models for compositional and network data, as cited in the work.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Fang, H.; Huang, C.; Zhao, H.; Deng, M. gCoda: Conditional Dependence Network Inference for Compositional Data. Journal of Computational Biology, 2017.

name.justification: These correlation methods are specifically proposed for prediction on test data and training with cross-validation in the paper.
name.quote: Introducing new techniques for leveraging well-established algorithms such as Pearson/Spearman correlation.

is_contributed.justification: While Pearson and Spearman correlation themselves are established methods, their novel application using the new cross-validation technique presented in the paper is a contribution.
is_contributed.quote: We propose training the optimum correlation threshold in correlation-based algorithms with cross-validation.

is_executed.justification: Pearson and Spearman correlations are applied in the empirical analysis as described in the methods and results sections.
is_executed.quote: Implemented the Spearman algorithm by converting the data into ranks adopting the Pearson Correlation algorithm to predict the ranks.

is_compared.justification: These methods are compared with others like LASSO and GGM to analyze performance metrics.
is_compared.quote: From the graph, we can infer that the Pearson mostly has more number of edges than Spearman.

referenced_paper_title.value: Inferring Correlation Networks from Genomic Survey Data
referenced_paper_title.justification: The research relies on the methodologies developed in the referenced papers for Pearson/Spearman application.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Friedman, J.; Alm, E.J. Inferring Correlation Networks from Genomic Survey Data, 2012.

name.justification: Amgut2 is referred to multiple times as a dataset used for empirical testing of the proposed methods.
name.quote: The Amgut2 real microbiome dataset undergoes the Yeo-Johnson transformation and standard scaling before we conduct the cross-validation analysis.

referenced_paper_title.quote: McDonald, D.; Hyde, E.; Debelius, J.W.; et al. American Gut: an Open Platform for Citizen Science Microbiome Research.

name.quote: Results from Figure 4 show that the accuracy of the algorithms generally improved upon increasing the number of total samples using crohns dataset.

name.quote: The GGM outperformed the other algorithms on the iOral data set.

name.quote: In this study, we conducted a real microbiome composition data analysis on Amgut1.
